note: Hyperventilation is a recognised hallmark of dominant RNU2-2 DEE (present in 3/5 patients in Chiu et al. and highlighted in OMIM/PanelApp), making an estimated 35-60% prevalence across Leitão et al.'s 35 dominant cases highly plausible.

evidence.text: Chiu et al. identified RNU2-2 variants in patients with developmental and epileptic encephalopathy, finding hyperventilation in 3 of 5 assessed individuals.

source.title: Pathogenic Variants in RNU2‐2, a Non‐coding Spliceosomal RNA, Cause a Distinctive Developmental and Epileptic Encephalopathy
source.quote: Patients with RNU2-2 DEE had median seizure onset age of 24 months, focal and generalized seizures, status epilepticus (n = 5), severe to profound impairment, hyperventilation (n = 3), and obstructive sleep apnea (n = 3).

evidence.text: Leitão et al. analyzed 141 individuals with RNU2-2 variants, confirming a dominant cohort of 35 individuals with recurrent pathogenic variants.

source.title: Systematic analysis of snRNA genes reveals frequent RNU2-2 variants in dominant and recessive developmental and epileptic encephalopathies
source.quote: We report RNU2-2 variants in 141 individuals, including 35 with recurrent dominant pathogenic variants and 91 affected members from 73 families with biallelic variants.
